daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The secretaries-general of Prabowo's coalition parties gathered for reflection ahead of Indonesia's Independence Day, reinforcing coalition unity. Separately, PKB announced the formation of a Prabowonomics task force to supervise the president's economic agenda. The gathering comes as Prabowo is expected to announce teacher salary increases during his speech at tomorrow's annual parliamentary session.

  • PDI-P chairwoman Megawati Maharno stated that political parties require research and science, while Gerindra responded to her earlier assertion that PDI-P will not join Prabowo's cabinet.
  • DPR Speaker Puan Maharani told participants in the Youth Parliament program that the DPR is frequently targeted by hoaxes.
  • A DPR member called for teacher salary increases after education budget allocations were not used for the school meals programme.
  • Home Affairs Minister Tito Karnavian opened collaboration between ministries in recognising high-performing local governments at the 2026 awards ceremony.
  • An intellectual group issued a manifesto calling for Indonesia envisioned by the constitution.
  • The KPK searched the home of Bengkulu City councillor Vinna Ledy, and separately investigated non-budget funds in the Bank BJB advertising procurement case while declining to detain former Bank BJB president director Yuddy Renaldi after questioning him as a suspect.
  • The Constitutional Court rejected a challenge to regulations requiring late SIM renewals to be processed as new applications, with the ruling also closing opportunities for sympathisers to file frivolous reports about presidential and vice-presidential insults.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia condemned Israel's rejection of a roadmap for Gaza's recovery, with the Foreign Ministry issuing a formal statement of censure. The ministry also condemned a ship attack in Bab Al-Mandeb that left one Indonesian crew member missing and others injured, calling on authorities to provide assistance to the victims.

  • The United States declared readiness to cooperate with Indonesia in safeguarding territorial sovereignty while opening opportunities for new partnerships and affirming respect for Indonesian sovereignty.
  • Indonesia and Timor-Leste strengthened bilateral cultural cooperation through a formal agreement.
  • The Indonesian military targets 11,000 public facilities by year-end 2026, including the inauguration of 3,395 TNI-Polri bridges and 3,000 water sources.
  • Two young Indonesians represented the country in a UNESCO global programme.
  • The Foreign Ministry responded to Malaysian concerns about forest fire haze crossing the border.

Other

President Prabowo set a two million target for Indonesia's national electric motorcycles and inaugurated Molinas, the national electric motorcycle ecosystem, which he called an example of "Indonesia Incorporated". The initiative received backing from state holding company Danantara, which supports financing for the programme, with a minister identifying a US$170 billion potential market.

  • Customs authorities foiled a US$3.52 million gold smuggling attempt at Soekarno-Hatta Airport, while the Finance Minister suspects illegal gold mines supply smuggling syndicates exporting abroad.
  • Finance Minister Purbaya will impose export taxes on jewellery above certain weight thresholds.
  • MSCI dropped two Indonesian stocks from its flagship Global Standard Index, prompting the Indonesia Stock Exchange to maintain communication with MSCI after the August review.
  • Indonesia eyes 2028 for electric car mass production at a West Java manufacturing hub, while the UAE is exploring Masdar's involvement in an Indonesian dam project.
  • The National Nutrition Agency permanently closed 504 school meal kitchens that failed to meet sanitation standards and is targeting 658,300 teachers for nutrition education in the school meals programme.
